channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD approaches $4,300 after rejection at the $4,400 area
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades lower for the second consecutive day on Tuesday, extending its decline to levels below $4,320 during the European session, as the recovery attempt from last week’s low was capped at $4,400.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: NBH stance supports carry appeal – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky expects the National Bank of Hungary to pause its mini easing cycle at 5.50% and possibly outline a two-step cut in its inflation target from 3.0% to 2.0%.

item.title: US Dollar: Fed tightening keeps upside risks – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) is extending gains after the latest hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) hike, even as reopening prospects for the Strait of Hormuz temper the move and weigh on Oil.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Hawkish RBNZ pricing supports kiwi – MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Lee Hardman highlights the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) as the main overnight mover, boosted by hawkish guidance from Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) Governor Breman. His comments on higher Oil-driven inflation have reinforced expectations for a third consecutive 25 bps hike next month.

item.title: WTI falls to near $90.00 after news of Iran proposing reopening Hormuz
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) extends its losing streak after losing daily gains, trading around $90.20 per barrel during the European hours on Tuesday.

item.title: United States Dollar Index (DXY) eases from July 30 high as Iran offers to reopen Hormuz
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, retreats slightly after hitting a fresh high since July 30 during the early European session on Tuesday. The index, however, lacks follow-through and currently trades just below mid-100.00s, unchanged for the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Consolidation continues below resistance against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see AUD/USD consolidating around 0.7120 after a brief spike to 0.7140. Intraday price action is viewed as part of a 0.7105–0.7135 range.

item.title: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz Strait within 7 days – Kyodo News
item.description: According to a report from Kyodo news, a senior Iranian official has said that Iran will reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint to almost 20% of global energy supply, within seven days if the United States (US) takes initial steps toward easing military pressure.

item.title: Indian Rupee surrenders early gains, UN General Assembly awaited
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens higher again versus the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday but later gives back its early gains. The USD/INR pair flattens at around 95.82 ahead of meeting between leaders from the United States (US) and Gulf nations regarding the energy supply through the Middle East.

item.title: Euro hits fresh seven-week lows as German political uncertainty offsets risk-on mood
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is failing to draw any support from the moderate risk appetite triggered by the recent pullback in Oil prices and extends losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, hitting fresh seven-week lows below 1.1450.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD plummets below $65 on higher-for-longer Fed interest rates narrative
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is down 1.75% to near $64.85 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The white metal is under severe selling pressure as Federal Reserve (Fed) officials warn that strong demand is also fuelling upside inflation risks alongwith higher oil prices.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Hiking path constrained by supply shocks – BNY
item.description: John Velis at BNY Markets argues that current US inflation is being driven by non-rate-sensitive components of core PCE, limiting how effective further Federal Reserve tightening can be.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Rises to near 158.00 near 50-day EMA
item.description: USD/JPY gains ground for the third consecutive day, trading around 157.70 during the European hours on Tuesday. The currency pair is consolidating after the recent pullback while remaining capped by the medium-term trend filter.

item.title: Gold flirts with $4,300 as inflation fears reaffirm Fed bets and underpin bullish USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts follow-through selling for the second straight day, with bears now looking to extend the slide further below the $4,300 mark during the first half of the European session on Tuesday.

item.title: Forex Today: Geopolitical uncertainty keeps markets on edge
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Tuesday, September 22:

item.title: British Pound: BoE pricing keeps rangebound against Euro – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes EUR/GBP has held a tight 0.855–0.860 range since early September after a Bank of England (BoE) meeting that did not strongly challenge aggressive market tightening expectations.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Bulls retain control near August 6 highs, just below mid-1.4000s
item.description: The USD/CAD pair extends its consolidative price move through the early European session on Tuesday, trading below 1.4050, or the highest since August 6, amid mixed fundamental cues.

item.title: British Pound reverses earlier gains as UK Public Sector Net Borrowing surges
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) is giving back earlier gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as data from the UK revealed that public sector borrowing increased beyond expectations in August, rekindling market concerns about government finances.

item.title: Equities: Fresh optimism lifts S&P 500 near highs – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight a strong risk-on session in US equities, with the S&P 500 up over 1% and back in positive territory for September, sitting less than half a percent below its all-time high.

item.title: Dow Jones futures hold steady as traders await US-Iran diplomatic developments
item.description: Dow Jones futures inch lower by 0.04% to trade near 52,450 during European hours on Tuesday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures remain steady around 7,830, while Nasdaq 100 futures decline by 0.07% to trade near 30,760.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Range bias holds below resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) analysts Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann see USD/CHF trading with a mild downside bias in the short term, targeting support near 0.8190 while keeping 0.8155 intact.

item.title: Euro rises against Japanese Yen as latter underperforms across board
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is 0.2% at around 180.78 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Tuesday. The cross gains as the Japanese currency underperforms its currency peers.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: MNB pause supports HUF – Commerzbank
item.description: Antje Praefcke at Commerzbank highlights that the Hungarian Central Bank is widely expected to leave its key rate at 5.50% and possibly lower its inflation target to 2.5%.

item.title: British Pound remains on the front foot amid BoJ-inspired Yen weakness
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross scales higher for the third consecutive day – also marking the sixth day of a move up in the previous seven – and trades around the 210.75-210.80 region during the early European session on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro declines as US Dollar recovers recent losses amid hawkish Fed tone
item.description: EUR/USD remains subdued for the second successive day, trading around 1.1460 during the European hours on Tuesday. The pair faces challenges as the US Dollar (USD) recovers its daily losses amid prevailing hawkish sentiment surrounding the Federal Reserve (Fed) policy stance.

item.title: US Dollar: Stronger as Fed hike path extends – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman notes the US Dollar is holding a stronger tone after the Federal Reserve began tightening policy, lifting the Dollar Index back above 100.00. Support comes from a sharp rise in US yields, with markets now pricing three more Fed hikes over the next year.

item.title: Euro: Fair value drop points to downside against US Dollar – ING
item.description: Francesco Pesole at ING highlights that EUR/USD short-term fair value from the bank’s 60‑day model has fallen below 1.150, with equities and rate differentials driving moves more than Oil.

item.title: Euro weakens against Canadian Dollar amid German political turmoil, higher oil prices
item.description: EUR/CAD depreciates after three days of gains, trading around 1.6080 during early European hours on Tuesday. The currency cross is losing ground as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) draws strength on higher oil prices, which could be attributed to the heightened market caution.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Upside attempts likely to be tested at 0.5800
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) shows a modest recovery against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, favoured by somewhat brighter market sentiment as Brent Oil prices remain below the $100 level, which provides some relief to Oil-importing economies like New Zealand’s.

item.title: British Pound: Oversold slide nears 1.3335 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann remain negative on GBP/USD after the pair eased to around 1.3370. They expect a test of last week’s low near 1.3335, though a sustained break below that level and the major 1.3300 support is seen as unlikely.
